question.text: A company with paid-up capital of Rs. 8 crore and market capitalization of Rs. 30 crore applies for listing on NSE. The company has been profitable for the last 4 years. Which eligibility criterion is NOT met?

answer.text: Minimum paid-up capital requirement of Rs. 10 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: For NSE listing, paid-up capital must be at least Rs. 10 crore, the profitability track record must be at least 3 years, and market capitalisation must be at least Rs. 25 crore. The company meets profitability (4 years vs 3 years) and market cap (Rs. 30 crore vs Rs. 25 crore) but fails the paid-up capital test because Rs. 8 crore is below the Rs. 10 crore threshold. The Trap: Market capitalisation of Rs. 30 crore exceeds the Rs. 25 crore threshold, so candidates might focus on that and overlook the paid-up capital shortfall. Note: Minimum issue size is not an NSE-specific listing criterion in the workbook table; the NSE table covers paid-up capital, profitability, and market capitalisation.
